previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A man with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis was admitted due to persistent steal syndrome symptoms in his left hand despite prior fistula banding. He reported chronic coldness and severe pain during dialysis, requiring early session termination. Hypotension was noted, prompting temporary hold of diltiazem and isosorbide. After cardiology consultation, he was restarted on a lower dose of diltiazem and initiated on digoxin and midodrine before dialysis, which improved blood pressure and reduced steal symptoms. An arteriogram showed no major arterial blockages but persistent poor distal radial and ulnar artery filling, even after fistula compression and nitroglycerin. A healing, non-displaced mid-humerus fracture was incidentally found on X-ray, contributing to shoulder pain. He responded well to treatment, completed dialysis without pain, and was discharged to an extended care facility with medication adjustments, fistula monitoring instructions, and plans for digoxin level checks.

Brief Hospital Course:
Mr. ___ is a ___ year old gentleman with end stage renal 
disease on hemodialysis, type 2 diabetes mellitus, congestive 
heart failure, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, atrial 
fibrillation, history of GI bleed, AVG steal syndrome presenting 
with complaints of weakness. Hospital course complicated by Afib 
with RVR and labile blood glucose. 

BRIEF HOSPITAL COURSE
======================
ACTIVE ISSUES:
--------------
# Altered mental status/Weakness: Pt admitted with nonspecific 
symptoms, no objective fever/chills or signs/symptoms of 
infection. Neuro exam on admission nonfocal but diffusely weak 
and somnolent, suggesting metabolic toxic encephalopathy rather 
than structural component of altered mental status. CT head 
deferred. CBC without leukocytosis.  Persistently hypoglycemic, 
nadir blood glucose 29. Renal function panel and liver function 
tests were not suggestive of uremia or ammoninemia. Digoxin 
within therapeutic range. AMs and weakness most like drug effect 
v. recurrent hypoglycemia. Admission gabapentin downtitrated 
given ESRD, and insulin regimen changed to 10 U Lantus at night 
with low dose humalog sliding scale. Patient with marked 
improvement in altered mental status and strength after these 
measures, although still preferentially does not move left side 
secondary to pain.   

# Volume overloaded: Patient with signs and symptoms of fluid 
overload in the emergency department and on CXR. Patient taken 
to hemodialysis with clinical improvement.  

# AV graft Steal syndrome: Patient recently hospitalized twice 
in ___ for AVG steal syndrome. At this time, perfusion of the 
limb versus systemic hypotension was balanced.  He was started 
on digoxin and midodrine qHD which improved his blood pressures 
and decreased his steal syndrome symptoms during HD. This 
regimen was continued as inpatient. 

# Atrial fibrillation/AFlutter: Patient not on warfarin due to 
history of significant GIBs. Patien had episode of rapid 
ventricular response on day of admission, peak HR 170s, nadir BP 
___, denied chest pain throughout. EKG at HR ___pression in anterior leads. EKG at HR ___epression in V2-V4. Repeat troponin showed increased 
troponinemia from 0.40 --> 0.65, that plateaued, most likely 
rate related demand ischemia. Identified triggers: missed 
medication dose, hypoglycemia (blood glucse 29).   

#Thrombocytopenia: Mild, 120-140s throughout admission. Noted, 
etiology unclear. 

CHRONIC ISSUES:
---------------
# Mid humerus L fracture: Per orthopedic surgery, he does  not 
need further treatment for this fracture because it is  stable 
and healing well. It is non-displaced and not near a joint.

# Chronic Systolic and Diastolic Congestive Heart Failure: 
Patient with history of ejection fraction of 30%, improved to 
normal (60%)in ___. Admission weight: 76.5 kgs. Discharge 
weight 70.6KG.  

# End-Stage Renal Disease on HemoDialysis: Patient was continued 
on outpatient schedule ___. HD session was complicated by 
hypoglycemia (see above). Patient was continued on sevelamer, 
nephrocaps.

# Type 2 Diabetes complicated by peripheral neuropathy, 
retinopathy, nephropathy. Patient was continued on glargine with 
Humalog sliding scale. Gabapentin was withheld due to concerns 
for lethargy. Patient was continued on oxycodone for peripheral 
neuropathy.  

# Sleep Apnea: Recently seen by Dr. ___ as outpatient, d/t

continued on CPAP, chronic O2, home dose trazodone prn insomnia.
